messages:
morgan: quick check — I captured an nsys trace on rt-shard1 showing a kv-cache regression (warm vs cold mismatch). file is ~2.1GB. can't post raw traces to public, need scrub + consent before I upload to perf bucket. who can scrub & verify no PII? cc @sam @priya

sam: I can take a look. do you have the nsys cmd you used and the exact filename?

priya: also need to confirm inputs — was there any customer text in the input tensors or env logs? if so we need to redact or zero them before sharing.

morgan: no user text should be present, just model name in env and some debug logs. filename: rt1_kvcache_miss_2105557777.qdrep. capture command was:

```
nsys profile --output rt1_kvcache_miss_2105557777 --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none \
  --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-end=stop --force-overwrite --cpuctx-mode=cpu \
  -- python -m torch.distributed.launch run_infer.py --config run/rt1.json
```

perf-bot: auto: uploaded meta: size=2.1GB, events=5.2M, created=2105557777

sam: ok. plan: I'll run a scrub script to remove env vars and zero tensor buffers where necessary. rough steps:
- convert .qdrep -> .nsys-rep + raw slices
- redact env/args (grep & sed)
- zero large host buffers containing tokens
- regenerate a flamegraph svg from the scrubbed rep

jamie: one ask — when you regenerate flamegraphs please keep op names intact but strip model identifiers. we rely on op names for perf hotspots. also drop absolute file paths.

priya: we also need a quick PII check: run `rg "(email|ssn|social)"` and search logs for token-like strings. if anything hits, escalate to security.

sam: noted. i'll run the scrub now. if the final scrubbed rep is >1GB i'll produce a sampled rep + a lightweight annotated flamegraph to avoid S3 bloat. expected upload by EOD to the shared scratch path: s3://redwood-perf-scratch/anon/2105557777/ (ttl=7d).

morgan: perfect, thanks. after upload please paste the share link here and mark whether any info was redacted (model-name, file paths, etc).

sam: quick Q — should I also run an extra `torch.profiler` capture for the CPU part? might help correlate with host-side stalls.

priya: yes please — a small `torch.profiler` run for ~30s around the hotspot would be ideal. use `with torch.profiler.profile(..., record_shapes=True)` and attach the .pt trace.

sam: will do. i'll attach both the scrubbed nsys and the torch.profiler trace. ping me if you want to review redaction rules before upload. :thumbsup:

morgan: thanks all — tagging @perf-bot to note the thread. once uploaded i'll open a short doc with before/after flamegraphs and a summary of the suspected kv-cache behavior for the perf triage meeting.

perf-bot: note: perf job created #PJ-4512, owner=sam, due=2105559000

jamie: FYI if scrub process needs automation i can add a small Lambda to run the standard redaction steps and produce the sanitized artifacts. low effort.

sam: thanks jamie, might take you up on that. for now manual scrub + sanity check.

morgan: great. last_message: sam will upload scrubbed artifacts by EOD to s3://redwood-perf-scratch/anon/2105557777/ and will include an annotated flamegraph + torch.profiler trace. will follow up with a short doc. :pray:
